exchanges.subject: My car's value
exchanges.body:
Hi Maribel, I picked up my car and it looks great. But the dealer says it's now worth about $2,500 less because
it has an accident on its history report. Will Leon River pay me that diminished value?
Also, since the repair the blind-spot warning light on the right side keeps coming on by itself. Not sure if
that's related.
Allison Pruitt

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Hi Ms. Pruitt, I'm glad the car looks good. I understand the frustration about its history report. Your policy pays for direct loss to your car up to the lesser of its actual cash value or the cost to repair it; it doesn't pay diminished value, the loss in market value after a proper repair. Because this was a single-vehicle accident (the guardrail on SH 36), there's no other driver's insurance to make that claim against. Maribel Ochoa

threads.title: Simmons release: three problems before funding

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.subject: Simmons release: three problems before funding
exchanges.body: Rena, Paul: Keel's draft release has three problems against the demand we accepted (full release of Dale Prewitt for $30,000): (1) it reserves bad-faith and UIM claims against us; (2) it makes funds payable to the IOLTA only, while we have notice of Baylor's $3,210 hospital lien; (3) it adds an indemnity, which is fine for us. I'd ask Keel to remove the reservation (or confirm the insured is fully released regardless) and add Baylor as a payee or provide a lien release. Deadline pressure is theirs now since we accepted Wednesday, but I want this settled before Friday. Paul, could you look today?

exchanges.author: c_jennings
exchanges.body: This is Earl Jennings. Enterprise sent me a bill for ninety-eight dollars. Your company told me the rental was covered. I filed a complaint with the state about all this. Is somebody going to fix it?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: I'm sorry for the frustration, Mr. Jennings. Your policy's rental coverage pays up to thirty dollars a day, and the full-size car you picked was thirty-three fifty a day. We paid thirty dollars for each of the twenty-eight days, eight hundred forty dollars in all, and the ninety-eight dollars is the difference in the daily rate.

exchanges.author: c_jennings
exchanges.body: Nobody told me that at the counter.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Our letter of October 6th listed the thirty-dollar daily limit, but I understand it's easy to miss when you're standing at the counter. Our compliance team is answering the Department of Insurance with the full file. You're welcome to call me with anything else about the claim.

exchanges.author: c_jennings
exchanges.body: Alright. I'll pay Enterprise.

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Inbound 11/5 08:10. Insured upset about Enterprise's $98.00 balance; mentioned his TDI complaint. Explained transportation expense at $30/day: 28 days x $30 = $840.00 paid; $98.00 is the rate difference on the full-size car he chose ($33.50/day). Noted the 10/6 letter stated the limit. Told him Compliance is answering TDI; did not discuss the complaint further. He will pay Enterprise.

exchanges.author: c_danner

# LR-26-117563: medical records review (Sergio Villa), updated 11/5

Represented by Monique Hart (Hart Law Firm). Loss 7/18/2026, rear-ended by our insured; liability accepted.

| Provider | Dates | Billed | Paid (BCBS EOB) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Harker Heights Emergency Center | 7/18 | $2,140.00 | $1,284.00 |
| Killeen Spine & Chiropractic, 18 visits | 7/22-8/28, 10/14-10/30 | $3,960.00 | $2,376.00 |
| Central Texas Imaging (lumbar MRI) | 10/20 | $1,850.00 | $912.40 |
| Total | | $7,950.00 | $4,572.40 |

Recoverable medical expenses are limited to the $4,572.40 actually paid or incurred (Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code 41.0105).
Prior history: 9 chiropractic visits 3/4-5/2/2024 for low back pain after a lifting injury, discharged with intermittent symptoms.
Gap: 47 days (8/28-10/14) with no care; the lumbar complaint and MRI follow the gap and match the 2024 condition. Cervical strain (7/18-8/28 care) is related to our loss; the lumbar treatment after 10/14 is likely an aggravation at most, and arguably the prior condition.
Next: evaluate on the demand, weighting the cervical course (7/18-8/28) and discounting post-gap lumbar care. Reserve $10,000 remains adequate.
